Title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Untrusted RSS Feed in Jinja2 Template Rendering
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Details The `web/pandas_web.py` script parses external RSS/Atom feeds configured in `config.yml` under `blog.feed`. When parsing these feeds, it uses the `feedparser` library to retrieve entry details (such as `entry.title`, `entry.author`, and `entry.summary`), which are then inserted into the Jinja2 template rendering context. However, the Jinja2 environment is instantiated on line 452 without enabling autoescaping: ```python jinja_env = jinja2.Environment(loader=jinja2.FileSystemLoader(templates_path)) ``` In Jinja2, the `Environment` does not autoescape HTML/JS payloads by default unless `autoescape=True` (or a suitable autoescape selector function/extension) is explicitly passed. When rendering `web/pandas/community/blog/index.html`, the template inserts these values using `{{ post.title }}`, `{{ post.author }}`, and `{{ post.summary }}`: ```html
{{ post.title }}
Source: {{ post.feed }} | Author: {{ post.author }} | Published: {{ post.published.strftime(\"%b %d, %Y\") }}
{{ post.summary }}
``` Since autoescaping is disabled, if a malicious feed serves a post containing malicious JavaScript/HTML in `title`, `author`, `summary`, or `feed_name`, the injected scripts will be written directly into the generated HTML files without escaping, leading to a Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. ### Conceptual Exploit Payload A malicious RSS feed could contain an entry with a payload like: ```xml <script>alert(document.cookie)</script> Malicious Author <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> <iframe src="javascript:alert(1)"></iframe> ``` When `pandas_web.py` builds the website, it will parse this feed, generate the blog section, and write the unescaped script directly into `web/build/community/blog/index.html`. Any user visiting the generated blog page will execute the injected script.
